The NVDA close and prior close (USD 204.64 from 213.66) agree with the Twelve Data quote feed, and Yahoo Finance/Zacks (https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/stock-market-news-nov-2-132700821.html) and Ynet (https://www.ynetnews.com/business/article/ryivnsmazl) agree on Intel's guide (Q4 revenue USD 15-16B vs about 17.1B expected, EPS 25 cents vs 43 cents, blamed on PC weakness, memory prices and an Israel plant explosion) and on the same-day moves (Nasdaq -2.9%, AMD -10.9%, Marvell about -10%, TSMC about -6%, Broadcom about -5.5%). Intel's own data center revenue rose 78% to USD 7.3B (Ynet), so the guide gives no sign of weaker AI-chip demand. The coverage I read ties the drop to doubts about returns on AI spending after Alphabet's miss on Oct 29, not to anything about NVIDIA. Two side points, not scored as news: (1) a heygotrade note citing CNBC says NVIDIA's Intel stake lost about USD 6B on the day (USD 5B was invested in 2025; about USD 6B is consistent with a 29% fall on a stake worth roughly USD 20B); that is about USD 0.25 per share before tax on a non-operating mark, and I did not check whether NVIDIA's adjusted EPS excludes such marks. (2) The research set NVIDIA's exit multiple from peer multiples at the Oct 23 close; the same-day peer fall suggests that anchor is now lower. Rough sensitivity only, using one day of peer moves (about -8% on the peer median, NVDA's own multiple -4%): the exit multiple would go from 17.3x to about 16.4x, about -5% on the earnings-multiple leg and roughly -3% on the blended target. Offsetting longer-term point: the release names Anthropic, Meta, Microsoft, OpenAI and Oracle as running workloads on the first Helios racks (MI450 GPUs), so AMD is gaining a foothold at AI labs that are also Broadcom custom-chip customers. That is a share-of-wallet risk after the 12-month horizon as well as inside it; I did not mark it down for being late. What I could not size: how much of those labs' compute goes to AMD instead of Broadcom XPUs, and whether any Broadcom program is delayed or cut. The research's lab gigawatt haircuts (FY28 AI 195.5 billion versus the 230 billion line of sight) already carry some of this, and no Broadcom volume was cited. AMD's OpenAI tie is not new.

NVDA.summary: On Sunday Nov 8 NVIDIA's board said it is opening an independent investigation, run by independent directors with outside counsel, after reports that CEO Jensen Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence effort; Bloomberg and Axios headlines add that Huang admitted an affair. The board says it has no reason to believe national security or company secrets were compromised and that it has confidence in Huang, but the research did not model a probe into the CEO himself, and the stock fell 4.3% on Nov 9 (close 178.68) while the chip index rose. I cut the research target (12m) by about 4% as a best guess; this is not yet one of the listed triggers, and the Nov 17 earnings print is still the next hard test.
NVDA.fair_value_reasoning: Starting point: research target (12m) $263.97 (supervisor.json, engine: P/E leg weight 0.6 at 16.73x exit, FCF-yield leg weight 0.4). (1) Key-person tail: if the probe ends with Huang leaving or sharply cut back within the 12 months, I assume the target falls about 20% (loss of the founder's role in customer, supply and Washington relationships, plus a lower exit multiple). Probability I give that outcome: about 12% (board publicly backs him, says no sign of compromise, Huang is cooperating; but outcome unknown and Congress already asked for a briefing). 0.12 x -20% = -2.4%. (2) Overhang on the exit multiple: an open probe plus congressional and Commerce scrutiny lasting into 2027 justifies about half a turn off the 16.73x exit P/E, about -3% on the P/E leg, which carries 0.6 weight: -3% x 0.6 = -1.8%. Total about -4.2%, rounded to -4.0%, i.e. $263.97 x 0.96 = about $253.4. What I could not size: the probe's findings and timeline (none given), whether the foreign-intelligence angle triggers licence action against NVIDIA's Asian channel, and any customer reaction. Spot fell 4.27% on Nov 9 (186.64 to 178.67, Twelve Data), so the market has priced roughly the same size as my target cut, but a price move is not evidence. Details of the board statement come from one secondary summary (completeaitraining.com) plus Bloomberg/Axios/NBC headlines seen in search results; the full Bloomberg and Axios texts are unverified (fetch budget).
